_source: CHR 7.24.5 x86 MAC-Telnet console screens, captured 2026-11-26 over the L2 bridge (test/integration/mactelnet-l2-bridge.ts) with MacTelnetConsole.run() at the default 512 columns, during the review of #676 (#575). `command` is the exact text passed to run(); `raw` is the console's reply; `expected` is the command's output as the screen shows it (verified by hand: the echo, TAB completion lists and prompt redraws removed). In `wrap short output 473` and `474` the redraw fills the 512-column row, so the console wraps once more before the CRLF + CR that ends the echo; read on the screen alone, that wrap looked like a blank output line. Entries labelled `re-check:` are a second CHR 7.24.5 session (2026-11-26, same bridge and width) for the second review of #676: printed text that looks like the next command, ends with the command's own tail, looks like a prompt or a `{... ` continuation; repeated silent lines; a TAB-only line; a tail repeated at the wrap boundary; and `:put ""`. Their `expected` is the device output, set before the capture. Entries labelled `third (<version>):` come from the third review of #676 on CHR 7.24.5, 7.23.1 and 7.23.8 (long-term): command output that contains `ESC[9999B`, CR or CRLF + CR; a block and the next line in one call; and single output lines from 512 to 2049 characters, which the console wraps after 513 characters on the first row and 512 on later rows. Entries labelled `fourth (<version>):` (CHR 7.24.5 and 7.23.8 long-term) answer the CodeRabbit and tikoci/m2ir reviews of #676: wide lines that are not the first output line, two wide lines in a row, a wide line after a newline inside one printed value (its rows hold 512), spaces in the wrap column, and a printed `ESC[9999B[not-a-prompt`. Entries labelled `wide (<version>, <cols> cols):` come from a grounding run of real wide output on CHR 7.24.5 and 7.23.8 long-term at 512, 200 and 80 columns: print detail, tables, terse, as-value, export (verbose, terse), script and log listings, long lines exactly on wrap points, a newline inside a value followed by a long line, TAB and C0 controls. Each passing entry equals the same command over SSH exec with a matching width (`user+<cols>w`), or plain SSH for put-like output, apart from trailing spaces; RouterOS folds print and export to the terminal width itself, and that folding is kept. `cols` is the width the session negotiated.
